news.headline: PM Modi to visit Lucknow for National Skills Convocation, felicitate 52 toppers today
news.story_lead: PM Modi to visit Lucknow for National Skills Convocation, felicitate 52 toppers today PM Modi will felicitate 52 national-level skill-training toppers at the Fifth National Skills Convocation in Lucknow, his first visit to the city in nearly a year. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will attend the Fifth National Skills Convocation in Lucknow on Saturday evening and felicitate 52 All India Toppers, trainees who secured the first rank nationally in their respective skill-training programmes. This will be his first visit to the Uttar Pradesh capital in nearly a year.
news.full_article_text: PM Modi to visit Lucknow for National Skills Convocation, felicitate 52 toppers today PM Modi will felicitate 52 national-level skill-training toppers at the Fifth National Skills Convocation in Lucknow, his first visit to the city in nearly a year. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will attend the Fifth National Skills Convocation in Lucknow on Saturday evening and felicitate 52 All India Toppers, trainees who secured the first rank nationally in their respective skill-training programmes. This will be his first visit to the Uttar Pradesh capital in nearly a year. Although officially billed as a non-political event, the convocation comes months ahead of the 2027 assembly elections, giving the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) an opportunity to reach out to young voters in the state. Among the meritorious students to be feted, 37 are trainees from the All India Craftsmen Training Scheme (CTS) and 15 are trainees from the Craftsmen Instructor Training Scheme (CITS). Six meritorious trainees from Uttar Pradesh will also be honoured at the national level, including three CTS and three CITS trainees. Deep Dive Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship, Jayant Chaudhary, will also attend as special guests. In addition to the 52 awardees, 4,200 trainees and 209 trainers will also participate in the national event. State Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Vocational Education, Skill Development, and Entrepreneurship, Kapil Dev Agarwal, said that the national event, which was held in New Delhi for four consecutive years from 2022 to 2025, is being hosted outside the national capital for the first time, with Uttar Pradesh having the honour of hosting it. He said that under the vision of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the able leadership of Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, Uttar Pradesh is continuously achieving new milestones in the field of skill development and employment generation. He added that the selection of six young people from Uttar Pradesh among the 52 trainees to be honoured at the national level reflects the strengthening of the skill training system in the state and the increasing technical proficiency of the youth. The achievements of three trainees from the Regional Staff Training and Research Centre in Aliganj, Lucknow, will be a special highlight for the state at this event. The Regional Staff Training and Research Centre in Aliganj, which has been operating under the Uttar Pradesh government since 2015, is currently providing high-level training in 23 trades under the CITS scheme.

news.headline: Supreme Court Orders States to Immediately Set Up Wetland Grievance Redressal Committees
news.story_lead: The Supreme Court of India has directed all state governments to immediately establish four-member grievance committees under the Wetlands (Conservation and Management) Rules, 2017. The directive aims to address persistent public complaints regarding illegal encroachments on wetlands and ensure strict implementation of previous judicial orders on water body conservation.
news.full_article_text:
Environment & Wildlife: Supreme Court Mandates Wetland Grievance Committees

In a major push toward water body preservation, a Supreme Court bench comprising Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M. Pancholi directed all state governments to immediately form grievance redressal committees as mandated by the Wetlands (Conservation and Management) Rules, 2017. The ruling came during the hearing of a batch of public interest petitions filed by birder Anand Arya, advocate M.K. Balakrishnan, and environmental NGO Vanashakti, highlighting that states have failed to demarcate and protect designated wetlands even nine years after the notification of the 2017 Rules.

Key Directives and Statutory Framework:
• Statutory Mandate: Senior advocate Jayant Bhushan, serving as amicus curiae, pointed out that Rule 5(6)(b) of the 2017 Rules stipulates the creation of a four-member grievance committee. This panel is tasked with receiving public grievances regarding wetland encroachments and forwarding them to the respective State Wetland Authorities. The rules mandate setting up these committees within 90 days of the framework becoming operational.
• Court Orders: The Supreme Court observed that despite explicit protection orders, identified wetlands continue to suffer from encroachments. The bench instructed chief secretaries of all states for immediate implementation and scheduled the next progress hearing for December 2.
• Judicial Nexus with Article 21: In an earlier order passed on October 12, the apex court affirmed that protecting natural water bodies as sources of drinking water is fundamentally linked to the Right to Life guaranteed under Article 21 of the Constitution of India.

Wetland Inventory and Conservation Status:
• SAC Atlas 2021 Data: The Space Application Centre (SAC) Atlas 2021 mapped 231,195 wetlands measuring over 2.25 hectares, alongside 555,557 smaller wetlands under 2.25 hectares across the country.
• Ground Truthing & Demarcation: According to data submitted by the Union Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), physical verification (ground truthing) is complete for nearly 80% of wetlands (>2.25 hectares), and boundary demarcation is finished for nearly 95,000 wetlands.
• National Statistics: India currently has 1,319 officially notified wetlands and 103 designated Ramsar sites of international importance.

In December 2024, the court set a three-month deadline for states to complete boundary demarcation for wetlands listed in the 2021 Space Application Centre Atlas, though deadlines have seen repeated extensions.

जल निकायों के संरक्षण की दिशा में एक बड़ा कदम उठाते हुए, न्यायमूर्ति अरविंद कुमार और न्यायमूर्ति विपुल एम. पंचोली की पीठ ने सभी राज्य सरकारों को आर्द्रभूमि (संरक्षण और प्रबंधन) नियम, 2017 के तहत तुरंत शिकायत निवारण समितियां गठित करने का निर्देश दिया। यह फैसला पर्यावरणविद् आनंद आर्य, अधिवक्ता एम.के. बालकृष्णन और गैर-सरकारी संगठन वनशक्ति द्वारा दायर जनहित याचिका पर सुनवाई के दौरान आया, जिसमें बताया गया कि 2017 के नियमों को लागू हुए नौ साल बीत जाने के बाद भी राज्य आर्द्रभूमियों का सीमांकन करने में विफल रहे हैं।

मुख्य निर्देश और वैधानिक ढांचा:
• वैधानिक जनादेश: न्याय मित्र (एमिकस क्यूरी) के रूप में अदालत की सहायता कर रहे वरिष्ठ अधिवक्ता जयंत भूषण ने ध्यान दिलाया कि 2017 के नियमों का नियम 5(6)(b) चार सदस्यीय शिकायत समिति के गठन का प्रावधान करता है। इस समिति का काम जनता द्वारा उठाई गई शिकायतों को सुनना और उन्हें राज्य आर्द्रभूमि प्राधिकरणों को भेजना है। नियमों के तहत इन समितियों का गठन नियम लागू होने के 90 दिनों के भीतर किया जाना था।
• अदालत का आदेश: सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने टिप्पणी की कि अदालती आदेशों से संरक्षित आर्द्रभूमियों पर भी लगातार अतिक्रमण हो रहा है। पीठ ने सभी राज्यों के मुख्य सचिवों को इस आदेश के तत्काल कार्यान्वयन का निर्देश दिया और मामले की अगली सुनवाई 2 दिसंबर को तय की।
• अनुच्छेद 21 के साथ न्यायिक संबंध: 12 अक्टूबर को पारित एक पिछले आदेश में, सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने पुष्टि की थी कि पेयजल के स्रोत के रूप में जल निकायों का संरक्षण भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 21 के तहत जीवन के अधिकार से सीधे जुड़ा हुआ है।

आर्द्रभूमि सूची और संरक्षण स्थिति:
• एसएसी एटलस 2021 डेटा: स्पेस एप्लीकेशन सेंटर (SAC) एटलस 2021 ने 2.25 हेक्टेयर से अधिक की 2,31,195 आर्द्रभूमियों और 2.25 हेक्टेयर से छोटी 5,55,557 आर्द्रभूमियों को सूचीबद्ध किया है।
• ज़मीनी सत्यापन और सीमांकन: केंद्रीय पर्यावरण, वन और जलवायु परिवर्तन मंत्रालय (MoEFCC) द्वारा प्रस्तुत आंकड़ों के अनुसार, 2.25 हेक्टेयर से बड़ी 80% आर्द्रभूमियों का भौतिक सत्यापन (ग्राउंड ट्रुथिंग) पूरा हो चुका है, और लगभग 95,000 आर्द्रभूमियों की सीमांकन प्रक्रिया समाप्त हो चुकी है।
• राष्ट्रीय आंकड़े: भारत में वर्तमान में 1,319 अधिसूचित आर्द्रभूमियां और 103 अंतरराष्ट्रीय महत्व के रामसर स्थल मौजूद हैं।

hindi_translation.story_lead: यूक्रेन में जारी युद्ध के बीच पोलैंड के क्षेत्र में रूसी मिसाइलों के गिरने की खबरों के बाद यूरोपीय नेताओं ने तीव्र आक्रोश और चिंता व्यक्त की है। यह घटना क्षेत्रीय सुरक्षा के दृष्टिकोण से एक महत्वपूर्ण मोड़ है।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
### घटना का विवरण: पोलिश क्षेत्र में मिसाइल का गिरना
यूक्रेन में चल रहे सैन्य संघर्ष के दौरान रूसी हमलों से जुड़ी मिसाइलों के पोलैंड की सीमा के भीतर गिरने पर यूरोपीय राजनीतिक नेतृत्व ने कड़ी निंदा और चिंता व्यक्त की। यह घटना उत्तर अटलांटिक संधि संगठन (नाटो) की पूर्वी सीमा पर सुरक्षा जोखिम बढ़ाती है।

### प्रमुख तथ्य
- **स्थान:** पोलैंड, जो मध्य यूरोप का एक देश है और यूक्रेन की सीमा से सटा हुआ है तथा नाटो एवं यूरोपीय संघ का सदस्य है।
- **घटना:** यूक्रेन युद्ध के दौरान पोलिश भूमि पर मिसाइल का गिरना।
- **अंतर्राष्ट्रीय प्रतिक्रिया:** यूरोपीय देशों द्वारा घटना की कड़ी निंदा और सुरक्षा को लेकर चिंता।
bullet_points: यूक्रेन पर हमलों के दौरान रूसी मिसाइलें पोलैंड की सीमा में गिरीं।
यूरोपीय नेताओं ने घटना पर आक्रोश और गंभीर चिंता व्यक्त की।
पोलैंड नाटो और यूरोपीय संघ दोनों का सदस्य देश है।
इस घटना से पूर्वी यूरोप में सुरक्षा संबंधी चिंताएं बढ़ गई हैं।
यह घटना युद्धग्रस्त क्षेत्रों से सटे देशों के सुरक्षा जोखिमों को उजागर करती है।

news.full_article_text: India contacts Qatar over health of former Navy officer Purnendu Tiwari after hospitalisation India has contacted Qatar over detained ex-Navy officer Purnendu Tiwari’s health after reports he was hospitalized, urging proper medical care. India said on Friday that it had taken steps to ensure the well-being of a former Indian Navy official detained in Qatar following reports that he had fallen ill and been hospitalised in the West Asian country. Commander (retired) Purnendu Tiwari was among eight former Indian Navy personnel arrested by Qatari authorities on charges of espionage in 2022. The men, including highly decorated officers, were sentenced to death in 2023, but this was subsequently commuted by a Qatari court. The eight men were released on the Qatari Amir’s orders in February 2024, and seven of them returned to India, while Tiwari was detained and sentenced in a separate case. “We have seen some media reports on [Tiwari’s] health condition. We have gotten in touch with the Qatari authorities so as to ascertain his well-being, as also to impress upon them that if there is a requirement of him getting proper medical attention, that should be given to him,” external affairs ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal told a regular media briefing. “We also understand that he was recently hospitalised and we are seeking further details in regard to his medical condition,” he said. “We remain committed to doing our best for Commander Tiwari and we are in touch with his family members as also with the Qatari authorities.” People familiar with the matter said the second case against Tiwari focused on financial irregularities related to his former employer, a subsidiary of Oman-based Dahra Engineering & Security Services, which provided training and other services to Qatar’s armed forces. The detention of the eight men had strained India-Qatar ties for several months before the two sides were able to resolve the first case, which involved allegations of espionage. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Rezaul H Laskar Rezaul Hasan Laskar is Foreign Editor with the Hindustan Times, which he joined in 2015. He began as a journalist in his hometown of Shillong in northeast India and has worked in newspapers and wire services over the years. He moved to New Delhi in 1997 and initially focused on defence, national security, Jammu and Kashmir and the northeast, while also working of foreign policy and international relations. He has been part of the media delegation accompanying PMs on foreign visits and has reported from destinations ranging from Tibet to Ukraine. Between 2007 and 2013, he was the Press Trust of India correspondent in Pakistan, one of only two Indian journalists allowed to report from the country. He extensively covered Pakistan’s domestic politics and the life of the common people, as well as the fallout of the 2008 Mumbai attacks on India-Pakistan relations and the subsequent trial in Pakistan of the suspects involved in the attack. As part of his reportage in Pakistan, he travelled the breadth of the country, from the Swat Valley to Balochistan. “We also understand that he was recently hospitalised and we are seeking further details in regard to his medical condition,” he said. “We remain committed to doing our best for Commander Tiwari and we are in touch with his family members as also with the Qatari authorities.”

People familiar with the matter said the second case against Tiwari focused on financial irregularities related to his former employer, a subsidiary of Oman-based Dahra Engineering & Security Services, which provided training and other services to Qatar’s armed forces.

Union agriculture and farmers’ welfare and rural development minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan unveiled the vaccine. Describing animal husbandry and poultry as vital pillars of the rural economy, Chouhan said livestock function as “moving ATMs” for farmers, providing a regular source of income alongside agriculture. “Animal husbandry contributes 14% to India’s GDP, while the poultry sector accounts for another 1 per cent. Foot-and-mouth disease causes average annual losses of ₹ 22,000 crore, Lumpy Skin Disease results in losses of ₹ 20,000 crore, Brucellosis accounts for ₹ 9,212 crore and Peste des Petits Ruminants, a disease affecting sheep and goats, causes losses of ₹ 4,683 crore. Together, these diseases have caused losses of approximately ₹ 56,000 crore to the country and its farmers. Indigenous vaccines are playing a crucial role in protecting livestock, safeguarding farmers’ incomes and reducing this economic burden,” he said. The research team comprised Dr S Nagarajan, Dr Manoj Kumar, Dr C Tosh, Dr H.V. Murugkar, Dr Aniket Sanyal, Dr Senthil Kumar D., Dr Naveen Kumar and Dr Yogisharadhya R. A scientist at NIHSAD said, “The vaccine, priced at ₹ 1-2 per dose, is the world’s first vaccine against this particular variant of bird flu. It is expected to strengthen disease prevention in the poultry sector, protect the livelihoods of millions of poultry farmers and help reduce the enormous economic losses caused by animal diseases.” Highlighting the efforts behind the breakthrough, Chouhan said the achievement belonged to the scientists and deserved recognition at the very place where the vaccine was developed. The scientists worked under stringent biosafety protocols throughout the research period. As part of these measures, they had to undergo sanitisation procedures before and after leaving the laboratory, use nearly 120 litres of water daily for bathing, and refrain from keeping pets at home during the course of the research. The need for effective preventive measures against bird flu has grown over the years. India’s first bird flu outbreak was reported in Navapur, Maharashtra, in 2006, resulting in the death of nearly one million chickens. To contain the infection, lakhs of other birds were also culled and buried. Since then, India has witnessed more than 500 bird flu outbreaks, causing significant damage to the poultry industry. Around nine lakh chickens died in 2021, while another two lakh birds have died this year. The disease also poses a risk of transmission to mammals and humans, making effective prevention and control measures particularly important. Chouhan also announced the establishment of a new state-of-the-art laboratory in Bhopal at an estimated cost of ₹ 300 crore. Address the gathering, the minister took a swipe at Opposition leaders for allegedly questioning India’s constitutional institutions and scientific capabilities while speaking abroad. Without naming Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, he said those who travel overseas and criticise the country should take note of India’s achievements and growing scientific strength. “The people who hold constitutional positions but question the Constitution abroad, undermine constitutional institutions and cast doubts on the contribution of India’s armed forces, scientists and hardworking citizens must look at the changing India of today,” he said.

A severe drought that began in April has destroyed crops, while food brought in from elsewhere has become increasingly unaffordable. "Seven months without rain has brought us to this point where we now live in hunger," the 44-year-old farmer, who lives with his grandmother, wife and five children, told the BBC. "Even some of the wild plants that we used to eat have withered and dried up." Local officials say more than 90% of crops have failed in the region, where agriculture is largely rain-fed. Further south, in Malawi, Mathews Nkhambala has experienced the devastating effects of flooding. In April 2024, barely a year after Tropical Cyclone Freddy devastated the country's southern region, floods displaced people in Chikwawa district. Nkhambala fled to higher ground with his wife and four children as floodwaters swept through his village. "As we reached a safe height, we saw our house swept away right in front of our eyes. Everything I had was gone," he told the BBC. He lost a harvest of 15 bags of sorghum and part of his farmland. His children were so traumatised that they stopped going to school. "They refused to go to school for many months. They were so disturbed," he recalled. After relocating and trying to rebuild his life, Nkhambala is now facing another climate challenge - this time a lack of rain. "This time we fear there may be no harvest. I have no clue what I will do." A government assessment after Cyclone Freddy found that Malawi had experienced more than 50 disasters linked to storms, floods, landslides and droughts since 1980, affecting millions of people. While Uganda and Malawi are suffering the effects of climate change and their governments are asking for assistance adapting to the new global weather patterns, they are among 23 African countries yet to submit National Adaptation Plans (NAPs) to the UN climate convention secretariat. These are the plans that detail how climate change has affected them and the risks they face, and so help make a case for what assistance they need. Without them, experts say, it becomes difficult to secure funding. "Our region has experienced cyclical droughts for decades, but there has been no action plan to tackle these climate impacts," said Milton Lorpia, who works for Warrior Squad Foundation in Karamoja region of Uganda. "If only such a plan were in place and implemented, it would certainly have helped us." Mathews Nkhambala and his wife fear their harvest may fail this year The African Group of Negotiators at the ongoing UN climate summit (COP31) in Turkey is pushing for adaptation finance to be tripled by 2035, from an annual $40bn (Â£30bn) baseline that it says developed countries committed to providing by 2025. The interpretation of that commitment remains contested. The proposal was not accepted for formal negotiations at the summit, although African negotiators have continued to push for it. The funding is intended to help vulnerable countries prepare for and withstand climate change-induced extreme weather, such as droughts, floods and wildfires. But the European Union, one of the largest providers of climate finance, says the priority should be ensuring existing commitments reach vulnerable countries rather than setting new funding targets. "We haven't come to the table with additional monies or additional capital. It's about what we have committed already and ensuring it's deployed," Darragh O'Brien, who leads the EU delegation at COP31 on behalf of the Irish presidency of the Council of the EU, told a press conference. He acknowledged that developing countries faced difficulties accessing available funding, saying the process needed to be improved. Wopke Hoekstra, the European Commission's climate commissioner, also argued that the summit should focus on delivering existing pledges rather than making new ones. "If you are a vulnerable nation in the Pacific or one of the LDCs (Least Developed Countries) and the money is in the bank but does not land on the ground then it is effectively meaningless," he said. - 'It can kill us': Kenyans fear impact of El NiÃ±o with floods predicted Published 11 November - A really simple guide to climate change Published 6 November Hoekstra said the EU had provided $30bn of the $100bn in climate finance committed by developed countries in recent years, adding that other wealthy nations should contribute more. The scale of the need is substantial. According to the UN's Adaptation Gap Report published last year, sub-Saharan Africa requires about $51bn annually in adaptation finance, while the Middle East and North Africa needs $112bn. Globally, developing countries will need about $300bn annually by 2035, according to the UN's latest report. Yet they received only about 10% of that amount from developed countries in 2024. Climate-related loss and damage in Africa is projected to cost $440bn between 2020 and 2030, according to Nairobi-based think tank Power Shift Africa. Under the 2015 Paris climate agreement, developed countries are required to provide financial support to developing nations, including for climate adaptation. But why have so many African countries failed to prepare plans that could help them identify their needs and build resilience? "If you look closely, the countries that are yet to submit their NAPs are already dealing with multiple crises, including debt distress, economic pressures and other issues," said David Abudho, climate justice lead at the aid agency, Oxfam. "Their governments' ability to invest in climate adaptation is limited." news.story_lead: Sean Cairncross (left) was appointed by the Trump administration - Published 20 November 2026, 09:37 GMT The top cyber-security official in the US government is leaving his post after a little over a year in the job. White House National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross was fired after losing the confidence of the White House chief of staff, Stephen Miller, according CBS, the BBC's US news partner. Asked about his removal on Friday, President Donald Trump said it was because he was not "good enough".
news.full_article_text: Sean Cairncross (left) was appointed by the Trump administration - Published 20 November 2026, 09:37 GMT The top cyber-security official in the US government is leaving his post after a little over a year in the job. White House National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross was fired after losing the confidence of the White House chief of staff, Stephen Miller, according CBS, the BBC's US news partner. Asked about his removal on Friday, President Donald Trump said it was because he was not "good enough". His firing comes after a string of tech outages which hit banking, air traffic control and other sectors. US officials said the outages were not caused by cyberattacks but the blackouts had sparked scrutiny from members of Congress who demanded a clearer explanation of what went wrong. There has been no official confirmation of the removal of Cairncross but Secretary of State Marco Rubio posted on X , external to say Department of Defense chief information officer Kirsten Davies was the new national cyber director. The news, first reported by Axios , external , follows security concerns, including the ability of advanced AI models - mostly from US companies - to discover vulnerabilities which humans would not be able to find on their own. Earlier this week, Rubio said there was "zero evidence" the outages were connected, adding "we are not under systemic attack". But the fact that so many have happened in quick succession has left some people worried about the safety of the tech which is heavily relied on in all aspects of daily life. - Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages? Published 2 days ago Cairncross was previously a lawyer in the Republican Party, before becoming the chief operating officer of the Republican National Committee. In the first Trump administration, he was part of the team of the White House chief of staff. news.headline: Anthropic shares fall after blockbuster opening as wider tech sell-off continues
news.story_lead: Watch: How did Anthropic's stock market debut unfold? - Published 20 November 2026, 14:36 GMT Anthropic's shares have dropped back towards their initial price after a soaring first day on the stock market, as a wider tech sell-off deepens. The fall in tech stocks continued to weigh on markets through Friday, with the S&P 500 down about 2.8% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average down more than 1% by mid-afternoon.
news.full_article_text: Watch: How did Anthropic's stock market debut unfold? - Published 20 November 2026, 14:36 GMT Anthropic's shares have dropped back towards their initial price after a soaring first day on the stock market, as a wider tech sell-off deepens. The fall in tech stocks continued to weigh on markets through Friday, with the S&P 500 down about 2.8% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average down more than 1% by mid-afternoon. Both US indexes touched correction territory, a point where they are trading at 10% or more down from a recent high. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite Index also fell more than 4% by afternoon trading as shares in major tech companies continued to fall. The speed at which AI investment has been growing - with more than $1 trillion spent in the last year alone by a small handful of major tech companies - has led to ongoing concerns of a financial bubble. Questions are being raised over whether those investments will pay off, and when. Despite a positive first day of trading, Anthropic's shares fell on Friday, dropping at one point by more than 12% to about $85, close to its initial public offering (IPO) price of $83. The artificial intelligence (AI) company's introduction to the Nasdaq stock exchange on Thursday was a crucial test for the industry and was largely seen as a success, with trading starting at $111.50. The maker of the Claude chatbot raised a record $81bn in its initial public offering (IPO), but its share price moved significantly in the first day of trading. The shares peaked at $115 on Thursday, before easing to end the day up 17% at $97.17. Analysts said volatility was to be expected in the first days or even weeks of Anthropic's trading, as the company was the first frontier AI firm to go public so had no direct peers. Some have also noted the similarities with Elon Musk's SpaceX, which at the time of its debut in June was the largest IPO on record. Shares in the rocket and AI company experienced large swings in its first few weeks of trading. Most tech companies see their shares fall after hitting the stock market, often after reporting quarterly results for the first time. But many, including Meta, Amazon and Google, have gone on to become the largest and most profitable corporations in the world. Ed Moya, a strategist at market intelligence firm AlphaSense, said Anthropic's blockbuster IPO did not appear to have restored confidence in the broader AI market. While AI demand was still very strong, Moya told the BBC that investors were trying to answer the question of how much were they willing to pay for that growth. "As we've gone through the past past few weeks, it seems that there's been more risks that have surfaced," he said. "Right now you're starting to see Wall Street is trying to shift from rewarding growth at any price, to demanding stronger cash flow and a clearer path to profitability." Shares in some of the largest US tech companies also fell on Friday as the market sell off continued. Nvidia shares had plunged by more than 11% by the afternoon, while Musk's firms SpaceX and Tesla had both fallen by more than 6%. Meta was down more than 5% and Amazon was down more than 3.5%, while Apple and Alphabet experienced smaller falls. Europe's main stock markets - which contain fewer tech stocks - also took a hit. Germany's Dax index closed down 2.6%, France's CAC 40 was down 1.9% and the UK's FTSE 100 ended trading 1% lower. Earlier on Friday, tech-heavy Asian markets saw steep falls. South Korea's Kospi and Japan's Nikkei 225 indexes closed down about 5%, with shares in memory chip makers Sk Hynix, Kioxia and Tokyo Electron, and other tech firms such as Samsung Electronics, seeing losses. Taiwan's stock market dropped about 6% on Friday, taking the weekly fall to more than 17% and what was reported to be its biggest weekly fall since 1990. news.headline: Russia Launches Massive Retaliatory Ballistic Missile Strikes on Kyiv Infrastructure
news.story_lead: Russia executed a widespread overnight missile attack targeting railway stations and strategic bridges in Kyiv, resulting in at least nine fatalities. The strike followed threats of retaliation from Russian President Vladimir Putin after Ukrainian forces severely damaged the Crimean Bridge. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky characterized the nationwide assault as one of the largest since the conflict began.
news.full_article_text:
### Russia-Ukraine War: Massive Retaliatory Strike on Kyiv Infrastructure

**Overview of the Attack**
In a major escalation, Russian forces launched a nationwide missile barrage overnight, focusing heavily on strategic civilian and transport infrastructure in Ukraine. Ballistic missiles struck key river crossings and bridges in the capital city of Kyiv, alongside railway hubs across the country. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky described the barrage as one of the most massive aerial bombardments recorded since the commencement of the war. Officials confirmed that at least nine people lost their lives during the overnight assault.

**Context and Retaliation Threats**
The strikes came days after Ukrainian forces delivered a damaging blow to the Crimean Bridge, a crucial logistics link constructed by the Kremlin following Russia's 2014 annexation of the peninsula to connect mainland Russia with occupied Crimea. Russian President Vladimir Putin had explicitly warned of direct retaliation against Ukrainian infrastructure following the attack on the bridge.

**Diplomatic Background**
The military escalation coincided with ongoing geopolitical discussions regarding potential avenues toward resolving the conflict. Concurrently, Kremlin officials rejected claims made by the United States suggesting that Moscow might be receptive to Western-backed security guarantees for Ukraine as part of any future peace framework.

hindi_translation.story_lead: रूस ने रात भर कीव में सामरिक पुलों और रेलवे स्टेशनों को लक्षित करते हुए देशव्यापी मिसाइल हमला किया, जिसमें कम से कम नौ लोगों की मौत हो गई। यह हमला यूक्रेनी सेना द्वारा क्रीमिया पुल को भारी नुकसान पहुंचाने के बाद रूसी राष्ट्रपति व्लादिमीर पुतिन की ओर से मिली बदले की चेतावनी के बाद हुआ। यूक्रेनी राष्ट्रपति वोलोडिमिर ज़ेलेंस्की ने इसे युद्ध की शुरुआत से अब तक के सबसे बड़े हवाई हमलों में से एक बताया।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
### रूस-यूक्रेन युद्ध: कीव के बुनियादी ढांचे पर बड़ा जवाबी हमला

**हमले का विवरण**
रूस ने यूक्रेन के नागरिक और परिवहन बुनियादी ढांचे पर रात भर बड़े पैमाने पर मिसाइल हमले किए। बैलिस्टिक मिसाइलों ने राजधानी कीव में प्रमुख नदी पार करने वाले पुलों और देश भर के रेलवे स्टेशनों को निशाना बनाया। यूक्रेनी राष्ट्रपति वोलोडिमिर ज़ेलेंस्की ने इस हमले को युद्ध शुरू होने के बाद से सबसे भीषण हमलों में से एक करार दिया। अधिकारियों ने पुष्टि की है कि रात भर हुए इस हमले में कम से कम नौ लोगों की जान चली गई।

**पृष्ठभूमि और प्रतिशोध की धमकी**
यह हमला यूक्रेनी बलों द्वारा क्रीमिया पुल को गंभीर नुकसान पहुंचाने के कुछ दिनों बाद हुआ है। क्रीमिया पुल 2014 के कब्जे के बाद क्रेमलिन द्वारा रूस को कब्जे वाले क्रीमिया से जोड़ने के लिए बनाया गया एक महत्वपूर्ण लॉजिस्टिक्स लिंक है। रूसी राष्ट्रपति व्लादिमीर पुतिन ने पुल पर हमले के बाद यूक्रेनी बुनियादी ढांचे के खिलाफ सीधे प्रतिशोध की चेतावनी दी थी।

**कूटनीतिक घटनाक्रम**
यह सैन्य हमला ऐसे समय में हुआ जब युद्ध को लेकर कूटनीतिक चर्चाएं जारी थीं। इसके साथ ही क्रेमलिन ने अमेरिका के उन दावों को खारिज कर दिया जिनमें कहा गया था कि मॉस्को यूक्रेन के लिए पश्चिम-समर्थित सुरक्षा गारंटी पर विचार करने के लिए तैयार हो सकता है।

यह सैन्य कार्रवाई ऐसे समय में हुई जब मॉस्को ने यूक्रेन के लिए पश्चिम-समर्थित सुरक्षा गारंटी के अमेरिकी सुझावों को खारिज कर दिया।

hindi_translation.story_lead: इजराइल ने 'सुपर आइस' नामक एक नई मिसाइल की जानकारी साझा की है, जिसमें पारंपरिक प्रणालियों की तुलना में चार गुना अधिक प्रहार क्षमता होने की बात कही गई है। यह तकनीक भारत की रक्षा आवश्यकताओं के संदर्भ में रणनीतिक रूप से महत्वपूर्ण मानी जा रही है।

इजराइल ने 'सुपर आइस' नाम की एक नई मिसाइल तकनीक के बारे में जानकारी दी है। यह हथियार प्रणाली पारंपरिक मिसाइल प्रणालियों की तुलना में काफी अधिक आक्रामक क्षमता प्रदान करने के लिए रेखांकित की गई है।

**तथ्यात्मक विवरण एवं भारत के लिए प्रासंगिकता:**
- **क्षमता**: 'सुपर आइस' मिसाइल में पूर्ववर्ती परिचालन प्रणालियों की तुलना में चार गुना अधिक प्रहार क्षमता ('4x द पंच') होने की बात कही गई है।
- **भारत के लिए उपयोगिता**: रक्षा विश्लेषण इस बात पर केंद्रित है कि यह प्रणाली भारत की सुरक्षा आवश्यकताओं के अनुकूल कैसे बैठती है और मौजूदा बेड़े में क्या रणनीतिक वृद्धि कर सकती है।
- **रणनीतिक मूल्य**: संवर्धित पेलोड क्षमता इस प्रणाली को आधुनिक स्ट्राइक तकनीक में एक महत्वपूर्ण विकास बनाती है।

इस मिसाइल में मानक मिसाइल प्रणालियों की तुलना में चार गुना अधिक प्रहार क्षमता होने की रिपोर्ट है।

news.headline: Russian Cruise Missile and Drone Violate Polish Airspace During NATO-Ally Exercise
news.story_lead: Polish authorities reported that a Russian Kh-101 cruise missile crashed in southeastern Poland near Nowy Lipowiec during a major Russian aerial assault on Ukraine. Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk characterized the airspace breach as a deliberate provocation, noting it occurred in proximity to the 11-nation 'Koalicja 2026' military exercise.
news.full_article_text:
### Russian Missile Incursion in Poland

On November 20, 2026, Polish defence officials confirmed that three airborne objects originating from Russia violated Polish airspace during one of Moscow's largest aerial bombardments against Ukrainian targets since the 2022 invasion. Among these objects, a Russian Kh-101 precision-guided cruise missile crashed at approximately 06:30 local time (05:30 GMT) in a rural area at Nowy Lipowiec, situated around 50 kilometers (31 miles) from the Ukrainian border. Polish Defence Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz detailed that a second suspected missile landed near Rudnik nad Sanem to the west, while a jet-powered drone crashed further south near Molodycz. No casualties or structural damage were reported.

### Context of Military Manoeuvres: Exercise Koalicja 2026

Prime Minister Donald Tusk stated that the incursion near Nowa Dęba was unlikely to be accidental, as it took place alongside 'Exercise Koalicja 2026'. Co-led by the United Kingdom and France, the military drill involves 11 member nations of the Coalition of the Willing rehearsing operational deployments in the event of a peace settlement in Ukraine. NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte condemned the severe breach of Polish airspace, confirming that alliance fighter jets were scrambled immediately in response.

### Allied Defense Response and Strategic Escalation

Following the incident, defence ministers from Poland, the UK, France, Estonia, and Lithuania toured the Nowa Dęba training site. UK Defence Secretary Wes Streeting framed the airspace violation as a targeted attempt to divide European allies and deter continued military assistance to Ukraine. European Council President António Costa reaffirmed European solidarity with Poland, urging Russia to enter diplomatic negotiations. The event followed a 40-nation Coalition of the Willing summit in Berlin, where German Chancellor Friedrich Merz advocated for early peace talks on neutral ground.

### Regional Impact and Historical Context

Russia's broader barrage targeted critical infrastructure across Ukraine, killing at least eight people in strikes on Kyiv's Dnipro River bridges and a railway station in Lviv. In parallel, Moldova reported its 118th airspace violation since February 2022 when a drone briefly crossed its border. Previous incursions into Polish airspace include a July 2026 cruise missile crash that created a 10-meter crater, and a November 2022 missile strike that killed two Polish farmers during an attack on western Ukraine.
news.background_context: The crash follows previous airspace incidents in Poland, including a July 2026 cruise missile impact leaving a 10-meter crater and a November 2022 missile explosion that killed two farmers. Moldovan authorities have separately recorded 118 airspace breaches since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

hindi_translation.headline: नाटो-सहयोगी सैन्य अभ्यास के दौरान पोलैंड के हवाई क्षेत्र में घुसी रूसी क्रूज मिसाइल और ड्रोन
hindi_translation.story_lead: पोलिश अधिकारियों ने बताया कि यूक्रेन पर रूस के बड़े हवाई हमले के दौरान एक रूसी Kh-101 क्रूज मिसाइल दक्षिण-पूर्वी पोलैंड के नोवी लिपविएक में दुर्घटनाग्रस्त हो गई। पोलैंड के प्रधानमंत्री डोनाल्ड टस्क ने इस घटना को जानबूझकर किया गया उकसावा करार दिया, क्योंकि यह क्षेत्र में चल रहे 11 देशों के 'कोअलिसजा 2026' सैन्य अभ्यास के पास हुआ।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
### पोलैंड में रूसी मिसाइल की घुसपैठ

20 नवंबर 2026 को पोलिश रक्षा अधिकारियों ने पुष्टि की कि 2022 के आक्रमण के बाद से यूक्रेन पर रूस के सबसे बड़े हवाई हमलों में से एक के दौरान तीन रूसी हवाई वस्तुओं ने पोलैंड के हवाई क्षेत्र का उल्लंघन किया। इनमें से एक रूसी Kh-101 प्रिसिजन क्रूज मिसाइल स्थानीय समयानुसार सुबह लगभग 06:30 बजे (05:30 GMT) यूक्रेन सीमा से लगभग 50 किलोमीटर (31 मील) दूर नोवी लिपविएक के एक ग्रामीण इलाके में दुर्घटनाग्रस्त हो गई। पोलिश रक्षा मंत्री व्लाडिसलाव कोसिनियाक-कामिश ने बताया कि दूसरी संदिग्ध मिसाइल रुडनिक नाड सानेम के पास गिरी, जबकि एक जेट-संचालित ड्रोन मोलोडीज़ के पास दुर्घटनाग्रस्त हुआ। इस घटना में किसी के हताहत होने या नुकसान की खबर नहीं है।

### सैन्य अभ्यास का संदर्भ: अभ्यास कोअलिसजा 2026

प्रधानमंत्री डोनाल्ड टस्क ने कहा कि नोवा डेम्बा के पास मिसाइल का गिरना महज एक हादसा नहीं लगता, क्योंकि यह 'कोअलिसजा 2026' अभ्यास के स्थल के पास हुआ। ब्रिटेन और फ्रांस के संयुक्त नेतृत्व में हो रहे इस सैन्य अभ्यास में 11 देश भाग ले रहे हैं, जो यूक्रेन में संभावित शांति तैनाती की तैयारी कर रहे हैं। नाटो के महासचिव मार्क रुट्टे ने पोलिश हवाई क्षेत्र के इस उल्लंघन की कड़ी निंदा की और बताया कि नाटो के लड़ाकू विमानों को तुरंत तैनात किया गया।

### अंतरराष्ट्रीय प्रतिक्रिया और रणनीतिक तनाव

घटना के तुरंत बाद पोलैंड, ब्रिटेन, फ्रांस, एस्टोनिया और लिथुआनिया के रक्षा मंत्रियों ने सैन्य प्रशिक्षण स्थल का दौरा किया। ब्रिटेन के रक्षा मंत्री वेस स्ट्रीटिंग ने इसे यूरोपीय सहयोगियों को विभाजित करने और यूक्रेन के समर्थन को रोकने की रूसी रणनीति बताया। यूरोपीय परिषद के अध्यक्ष एंटोनियो कोस्टा ने पोलैंड के प्रति एकजुटता व्यक्त की और मॉस्को से शांति वार्ता की अपील की। यह घटना बर्लिन में आयोजित 40 देशों के शिखर सम्मेलन के एक दिन बाद हुई, जहाँ जर्मन चांसलर फ्रेडरिक मर्ज़ ने तटस्थ क्षेत्र में शांति वार्ता की वकालत की थी।

### क्षेत्रीय प्रभाव और पूर्व घटनाएं

रूस के इस हमले में कीव में नीपर नदी पर बने पुलों और ल्वीव में एक स्टेशन को निशाना बनाया गया, जिससे यूक्रेन में कम से कम आठ लोगों की मौत हो गई। मोल्दोवा ने भी एक ड्रोन घुसपैठ दर्ज की, जो फरवरी 2022 के बाद से उसका 118वां हवाई क्षेत्र उल्लंघन था। पोलैंड में पहले भी ऐसी घटनाएं हुई हैं, जिसमें जुलाई 2026 में एक क्रूज मिसाइल दुर्घटना और नवंबर 2022 में दो पोलिश किसानों की मौत शामिल है।
hindi_translation.background_context: यह घुसपैठ पोलैंड में पहले हुई हवाई क्षेत्र की घटनाओं के बाद हुई है, जिसमें जुलाई 2026 में एक मिसाइल दुर्घटना और नवंबर 2022 में दो किसानों की मौत शामिल है। इसके अलावा, फरवरी 2022 से मोल्दोवा ने 118 बार अपने हवाई क्षेत्र का उल्लंघन दर्ज किया है।
bullet_points: एक रूसी Kh-101 क्रूज मिसाइल पोलैंड के नोवी लिपविएक में यूक्रेन सीमा से 50 किमी दूर गिरी।
दो अन्य संदिग्ध वस्तुएं (एक मिसाइल और एक जेट ड्रोन) भी पोलिश हवाई क्षेत्र में घुसीं।
पोलैंड में इस घटना से कोई नुकसान या हताहत होने की खबर नहीं है।
प्रधानमंत्री डोनाल्ड टस्क ने इसे 'कोअलिसजा 2026' सैन्य अभ्यास के दौरान किया गया उकसावा बताया।
अभ्यास कोअलिसजा 2026 ब्रिटेन और फ्रांस के नेतृत्व में 11 देशों का एक संयुक्त अभ्यास है।
नाटो महासचिव मार्क रुट्टे ने हवाई क्षेत्र उल्लंघन की निंदा की और लड़ाकू विमानों की तैनाती की पुष्टि की।
यूके, फ्रांस, पोलैंड, एस्टोनिया और लिथुआनिया के रक्षा मंत्रियों ने सैन्य स्थल का दौरा किया।
मोल्दोवा ने भी घटना वाले दिन अपने हवाई क्षेत्र के 118वें उल्लंघन की सूचना दी।

quiz.question: Which type of Russian cruise missile reportedly crashed near Nowy Lipowiec in southeastern Poland in November 2026?
